items.label: TSOL / Limousine Dream
items.genre: House, modular tech house, psychedelic house
items.context: Boulderhead appears on TSOL through Gene On Earth’s Limousine Dream storefront, pairing modular synthesis with changing arrangements and a prominent title-track vocal. The editions differ: “Throughout” is vinyl-only, while “Rounded” is digital-only.
items.dig_sentence: Then hear MINDHELMET 18 for another six-track view of Boulderhead’s dancefloor vocabulary.
items.why_candidate: High-priority club audition for the UFO Space, Cromby and chunkier-house side of the profile; count TSOL and Limousine Dream as one label family.

items.label: Fast At Work
items.context: Carsten Fluck and Lucas Lejeune bring their not even noticed project to Los Angeles imprint Fast At Work. Bass-led originals and spiralling acid are extended by contrasting K-LONE and Maara remixes, making the complete EP worth assessing beyond individual DJ tools.
items.dig_sentence: Follow remixer Maara into Ultimate Reward, her earlier release associated with naff.
items.why_candidate: Strong recent-crate fit and a new label route; this release remains eligible despite the separate exclusion of Beneath the Surface.

items.label: Couvre x Chefs
items.genre: Raptor house, tribal club, techno, trance
items.context: Caracas raptor-house pioneer Dj Babatr connects with French label Couvre x Chefs following a 2023 Paris performance. Four compositions from 2004 receive their first official release alongside contemporary remixes, linking foundational Venezuelan repertoire to a French club network.
items.dig_sentence: Then play Flow for a separate 2026 set of Babatr originals and an Awesome 3 reinterpretation.
items.why_candidate: High-priority club audition matching a heavily weighted recent artist while adding a different imprint and a specific archival story.

items.label: Unconfirmed; Alpha Tracks artist storefront
items.context: Kineta pairs Alpha Tracks and Oprofessionell, credited as Felix Benedikt and Filip Storsveen. Sold through Alpha Tracks’ artist storefront with no confirmed issuing imprint, this trilogy instalment offers three extended pieces rooted in concentrated Mediterranean recording sessions.
items.dig_sentence: Start the trilogy’s other available chapter with Proto I/III.
items.why_candidate: Catalogue wildcard for progressive-trance listening, with sustained development to assess; confirm the label before publication and exclude it from the confirmed-label count.

items.label: a.r.t.less
items.genre: Deep techno, Detroit-informed techno, ambient techno
items.context: Gerard Hanson’s Convextion project appears on a.r.t.less, part of Don Williams’ Mojuba label family, whose remit spans dancefloors and living rooms. Seven extended tracks, beginning with the sixteen-minute “New Horizon,” sustain a patient science-fiction environment.
items.dig_sentence: Then browse Mojuba’s catalogue, keeping a.r.t.less and its parent label together for quota purposes.
items.why_candidate: Aged-well alternative to an obvious Detroit-techno primer, bridging Aphex Twin, electro-adjacent futurism and colourful techno.

items.label: Die Orakel
items.context: Oliver Hafenbauer compiles upsammy, Pépe, Gacha Bakradze, Dana Kuehr, Poly Chain, Reptant and Edward for his Frankfurt imprint Die Orakel. Its genre-crossing electronic scope retains dancefloor purpose, with a digital programme broader than the four-track vinyl edition.
items.dig_sentence: Then hear Discotheque Saudades for a historical counterpart to this compilation’s melodic electronic curiosity.
items.why_candidate: Electro-forward discovery reserve with multiple routes outward; audition the full digital sequence before settling its club-versus-home role.

items.label: A Colourful Storm
items.genre: Ambient techno, melodic IDM, cosmic electronics
items.context: Jason Williams’s Velocette developed around Jonah Sharp’s Reflective label and his own Parallel imprint. Moopie’s compilation for A Colourful Storm revisits that West Coast intersection of Detroit-informed rhythm, melodic electronics and kosmische imagination, with Sharp’s recollections providing historical context.
items.dig_sentence: Next explore Headtravel, a Pacific Collective compilation that also includes Velocette.
items.why_candidate: High-priority catalogue discovery offering a less obvious route into Aphex, colourful-techno and cosmic-listening interests than a standard Warp introduction.

items.release: Where the Fields Never End : Revisited
items.label: Aleph Zero Records
items.context: Ooze is Sebastian Mullaert’s downtempo project, separate from Minilogue and Son Kite. Aleph Zero reissues his 2001 Spirit Zone album alongside reinterpretations by Koss, Porn Sword Tobacco, Bluetech and Minilogue, fitting the label’s ambient, dub and experimental-electronica remit.
items.dig_sentence: Then browse Aleph Zero’s catalogue for adjacent downtempo and electroacoustic releases.
items.why_candidate: Adventurous catalogue reserve connecting progressive trance with spacious home listening; audition carefully for dated psychill conventions.

items.label: Leaving Records
items.genre: Brazilian instrumental music, ambient jazz, acoustic/electronic
items.context: Rio-born, Los Angeles-based guitarist Fabiano do Nascimento extends Brazilian traditions into electronics and experimental composition on Leaving Records. Made with Daniel Santiago, the release combines several guitar types, upright bass and electronics while emphasising space and understated rhythm.
items.dig_sentence: Next play Solstice Concert to hear several related compositions in a different performance setting.
items.why_candidate: High-priority home audition bridging Os Tincoãs and Jorge Ben listening with ambient curiosity without relying on a canonical introductory Brazilian album.

items.label: FLAU
items.context: Cuushe’s release for Tokyo label FLAU centres on a lullaby created for a collaboration involving Daughter and photographer Kazuhei Kimura. Drawing on the historical Ryojin Hisho anthology, it follows one vocal idea through reinterpretations by Salamanda, Melati ESP and aus.
items.dig_sentence: Follow remixer Salamanda into the standalone vocal-focused piece Sing Together.
items.why_candidate: Short-form home reserve for Air, Domenique Dumont and warm-vocal listening, useful as a lighter alternative to another long ambient LP.

items.release: i was put on this earth
items.label: XL Recordings
items.genre: Experimental pop, ambient reggaeton, IDM, downtempo
items.context: Brian Piñeyro’s DJ Python project moves toward explicit songwriting on its XL Recordings debut, with Jawnino, Organ Tapes, Isabella Lovestory and Physical Therapy contributing. Piñeyro also sings, extending his atmospheric, melodic club vocabulary into vulnerable collaborative songs.
items.dig_sentence: Then hear Natural Wonder Beauty Concept, Piñeyro’s collaboration with Ana Roxanne.
items.why_candidate: High-priority home audition for DJ Lostboi, keiyaA and contemporary vocal interests; this established 2025 release clears the age gate unlike the newer follow-up.

items.label: Pink Oyster Records
items.context: Yejin Jang, also one half of Salamanda, releases this Yetsuby solo album through Pink Oyster, established by Jessie Goodchild and Métron Records. A childhood drawing informs themes of solitude and connection across dense melodic compositions drawing on ambient, bass and footwork.
items.dig_sentence: Compare the solo album with Yetsuby’s collaborative work on Salamanda’s In Parallel.
items.why_candidate: High-priority recent home audition for intricate electronics with warmth and melodic accessibility; consider choosing between this and Salamanda for artist breadth.

items.label: International Anthem
items.genre: Spiritual jazz, ensemble composition, electroacoustic interludes
items.context: Multi-instrumentalist Tomin Perea-Chamblee expands his homemade language of layered horns, jazz reinterpretations and electronics into ensemble performance for Chicago’s International Anthem. Players including Luke Stewart, Tcheser Holmes and Lester St. Louis bring cellos, low winds, keyboards and rhythm section into that framework.
items.why_candidate: Deliberate non-electronic widening of the pool for warmth, soul and immersive home listening; requires audition rather than assuming spiritual-jazz framing guarantees fit.

items.label: Outer Orbit Records
items.genre: Illbient, downtempo, leftfield techno, ambient, breakbeat
items.context: Dutch producer Spekki Webu revisits formative influences for new New York label Outer Orbit, following a connection through its sister party Mizz Softee. Illbient, trip-hop, lighter techno and ambient broaden his familiar intense dancefloor work; Cari Lekebusch contributes a vinyl-only remix.
items.dig_sentence: Then hear Ethereo Spatial Rift for a separate collaboration between Spekki Webu and Cari Lekebusch.
items.why_candidate: Strong 2026 discovery on a new imprint, potentially bridging both listening modes; audition the slower narrative first and note that four digital bonuses require full-album purchase.
